1.assumed: The watt is a joule per second: a unit defined from other units, not from quantities.

2.assumed: Work against weight uses only the vertical displacement moved.

3.assumed: Only transverse waves can be polarised, so rotating a polariser shows light is transverse.

4.assumed: Diffraction occurs when wavelength is comparable to the gap; electrons have a de Broglie wavelength near atomic spacing.

5.assumed: Infrared spans roughly 700 nm to 1 mm, so 50 µm is infrared.

6.assumed: a = F/m with constant mass, so acceleration has the same shape as the force graph.

7.assumed: For equilibrium, force vectors join tip-to-tail into a closed triangle.

8.assumed: Same load gives same force; elastic energy ½Fx is proportional to extension.

9.assumed: Divider current splits; find the p.d. across the load section, then P = VI.

10.assumed: Internal forces cancel in pairs, so with no external force total momentum is conserved.

11.assumed: Opposing e.m.f.s subtract; the larger drives the current; series current is the same everywhere.

12.assumed: Sum of currents into a junction equals sum out, using arrow directions.

13.assumed: For a quotient, percentage uncertainties add.

14.assumed: Maximum height after a bounce is where velocity is zero on the v–t graph.

15.assumed: Energy gained eV equals ½mv², so speed is proportional to the square root of voltage.

16.assumed: KEmax = photon energy − work function; then v = √(2KE/m) with electron mass.

17.assumed: Extension is inversely proportional to area; area scales with diameter squared; energy = ½Fx.

18.assumed: At the top only the horizontal velocity component remains, so KE = K cos²30°.

19.assumed: Parallel components share the same p.d., so P = V²/R is inversely proportional to R.

20.assumed: Angles are measured from the normal; n of glass about 1.5; apply n sin θ on both sides.

21(a).assumed: Mass is scalar and adds arithmetically; velocity is a vector so direction must be included.

21(b)(i).assumed: Weight acts vertically down; tension acts along the string away from the object.

21(b)(ii).assumed: From rest s = ½at², rearranged for t.

22(a).assumed: A systematic error shifts all points equally so the gradient is unchanged.

22(b).assumed: From v² = u² + 2as, gradient of u² against x equals 2a; then F = ma.

23(a).assumed: Pressure = weight/area; measure mass and diameter with suitable instruments; finer resolution improves precision.

23(b)(i).assumed: Archimedes: upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced.

23(b)(ii).assumed: Upthrust is the drop in apparent weight; displaced volume = upthrust/(ρ_water g); density = m/V.

24(a).assumed: Newton's second law in momentum form: resultant force proportional to rate of change of momentum.

24(b)(i).assumed: Momentum and total energy are always conserved even when kinetic energy is not.

24(b)(ii).assumed: Interaction forces are equal in size and opposite in direction at every instant.

24(c).assumed: Momentum is conserved; take a sign convention so rebounding velocity is negative.

25(a)(i).assumed: Both are energy per unit charge in volts; e.m.f. converts to electrical energy, p.d. from it.

25(a)(ii).assumed: Number density n = number/volume; then I = Anev solved for v.

25(b).assumed: Vary external resistance, record V and I, plot V against I: gradient = −r, intercept = ε.

26(a)(i).assumed: Points half a wavelength apart oscillate in antiphase, moving in opposite directions.

26(a)(ii).assumed: A loop is half a wavelength; v = fλ; percentage uncertainty carries through multiplication.

26(b)(i).assumed: Waves reflected at fixed ends superpose with incident waves to form a stationary wave.

26(b)(ii).assumed: One loop between fixed ends is half a wavelength, so λ = 2L.

27(a).assumed: Resistance = V/I at each point; negligible current means very high resistance; resistance falls as current rises.

27(b).assumed: An LED conducts only forward-biased above about its threshold voltage; cells in series add e.m.f.

27(c).assumed: Photon energy hc/λ; photons per second = power/photon energy, with mW and nm conversions.
